raw_response:
I'm 50 this year, been farming this land for 30 years. Never went to school, can't read the words on the fertilizer bags too well, but I know my 10.9 mu. Me and my wife, just us two now. The kids are in Shijiazhuang working factory jobs. They send a little money home at Spring Festival, but I can't count on it for seeds.

Most of my land, about 7 mu, I do wheat then maize. That's my backbone. Can't mess with that — if the grain fails, we don't eat. The wheat went in last October same as always. I used the regular seed, not that fancy new stuff my neighbor Wang tried. He said his yield was good but I don't trust it. I put one bag of compound fertilizer per mu in the furrow at planting, already done and paid for.

Now it's spring and the wheat is greening up. I need to topdress soon. Last year I got cheap and only used a little urea, and the wheat turned yellow before heading. Wang laughed at me. This year I'm doing the usual — half a bag of urea per mu when it starts growing fast. That's about 20 jin of the nitrogen stuff, or whatever the educated people call it. I just know it's half a bag, same as I've done for years that worked. I irrigate three times for wheat — once now at green-up, once when the heads are coming out, and once when the grain is filling. The well water costs money, they meter it now, but three times is necessary. Last August was dry and I only did twice, yield was down.

For maize, right after wheat harvest in early June, I got maybe one week to get it in. I buy hybrid seed from the shop, about 3 jin per mu. Costs more than saving my own but it grows better. One bag of compound fertilizer in the hole at planting. Sometimes I throw a bit more urea later if the leaves look yellow, but usually once is enough. Irrigate once or twice, depends on the rain in July.

The vegetables are where the cash comes from, but they're hard work with just two of us. I got 1.5 mu of watermelon, 1.2 mu of tomato, and 1.2 mu of eggplant. I buy seedlings from the market in Handan — don't have time or space to start my own. For watermelon I plant late April under plastic film. It needs water more, maybe four times, but sells good in July if the market price holds. Last year I got about 3000 jin per mu. I put chicken manure on the melon plot when I can get it from the chicken farm down the road, saves buying bags.

Tomato and eggplant are the hardest. Staking, pruning, picking every few days in summer. But the money is better than maize if bugs don't ruin it. Last year my eggplant got some wilt, so this year I'll spray more fungicide early. I hire a few days of labor for the tomato picking when it all ripens at once — me and the wife can't keep up. Hired hands cost 100 yuan a day now, so I only hire when I absolutely have to.

Cash is tight. I don't keep much in the house. The wheat fertilizer I already bought on credit from Old Li's shop. For the summer crops I need to save up from selling the wheat in June. If wheat price is below 1.2 yuan per jin, I'll have to cut back somewhere — probably buy less pesticide for the vegetables and hope for the best. I'd rather waste a little fertilizer than risk a bad yield. A bad year hurts more than a good year helps, that's what 30 years taught me.
